key_insight: Stabilizer syndromes of commuting Pauli rotations can be used as a unified design rule for constructing exact logical gates in both CSS and non-CSS quantum error-correcting codes.
engineering_relevance: This framework provides low-weight, physically implementable logical operations for fault-tolerant quantum architectures, including Clifford and non-Clifford gates on LDPC-style codes.
method: Derive an exact codespace-preservation condition for arbitrary rotation angles using syndrome structure.
Use an equal-syndrome specialization to reduce Clifford-gate design to stabilizer factorization and establish a generator-weight bound of ceil(d/2).
Extend the construction to higher-level logical rotations and implement explicit gates on BB, Mirror, recursive hypercube, and Reed--Muller codes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit constructions of low-weight gates such as addressed T, CCZ, CS, and C^rZ operations on several concrete codes, including cases that saturate the stated weight bound.
watch_item: The framework is structurally general, but practical fault-tolerance still depends on whether the derived low-weight logical gates can be realized with favorable error rates and control overhead on a given hardware platform.
paper_title: From Syndromes to Computation: A General Framework for Logical Operations in Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
